competitive_dynamics.tpd_class_density_2026: From NRC TPD review 2025 (10.1038/s41568-025-00817-8) B-cell malignancy is the SECOND-densest TPD oncology indication after prostate: 4 BTK PROTACs (NX-2127 triple-degrader + NX-5948 + BGB-16673 + ABBV-101; plus China-origin HSK29116/Haisco) + 2 BCL6 PROTACs (BMS-986458, ARV393) + next-gen IMiDs/CELMoDs & GSPT1 degraders (cemsidomide/CFT-7455, avadomide/CC-122, MRT-2359). BTK-PROTAC differentiation likely turns on linker geometry/TEC-family selectivity, E3-recruitment efficiency in B-cell compartments, and oral bioavailability; China-origin sponsors (Haisco, BeiGene/BeOne) are competitive in the subspace. BCL6-PROTAC win-condition = clinical benefit in ABC-DLBCL where direct BCL6 inhibition historically failed
competitive_dynamics.adc_ici_combinations_lymphoma_2026: From NRC ADC review 2025 (10.1038/s41568-025-00869-w) Lymphoma was the proving ground for ADC immunogenic-cell-death (ICD): brentuximab vedotin (CD30 MMAE) induced DC activation + CD8/NK recruitment + durable anti-tumour immunity in lymphoma models, with FcgammaR-mediated TAM uptake driving target-independent bystander killing. Clinically, BV + nivolumab + AVD in advanced cHL (Lee et al. Blood 2025) is one of the few proven ADC-ICI combos across oncology (alongside EV+pembro in urothelial). Read-across: positions CD30/CD79b/CD19 B-NHL ADCs (polatuzumab vedotin, loncastuximab tesirine) as legitimate ICI combination partners. Haematology ADCs also run LOWER effective doses than solid-tumour ADCs (fewer delivery barriers for B-cell tumours) — a structural advantage for CD79b/CD19 ADCs; loncastuximab tesirine (low-DAR ultra-potent PBD) exemplifies the design archetype (~50-200x lower dose), with the trade-off that PBD toxicity (vascular leak, transaminitis) does not transfer cleanly into combinations
competitive_dynamics.btk_degrader_class_phase3_2026: BTK degrader class confirmed Phase 3 (2026-06-08): Roche-Nurix bexobrutideg deal ($700M upfront, $2.3B total) marks the first BTK degrader Phase 3 entry with major-pharma anchor. Mechanism advantage: BTK PROTAC degraders eliminate BTK protein (C481-agnostic) vs covalent BTKi inhibition (C481-susceptible) or non-covalent BTKi occupation (C481-agnostic but reversible). Competitive read-across: (1) Lilly Jaypirca (pirtobrutinib) is the direct Phase 3 head-to-head comparator - if bexobrutideg shows superiority, Jaypirca's post-cBTKi niche is structurally threatened on a 3-5yr horizon; (2) AstraZeneca Calquence faces incremental long-term franchise erosion as the degrader class scales (AMPLIFY triplet is near-term response, doesn't address C481); (3) AbbVie/J&J Imbruvica already in structural decline post-ALPINE (zanubrutinib superior). Source: WS12 macro signals 146, 151. | BTKi GENERATIONAL LADDER (added 2026-06-11, Katie opt-augment): Gen 1 = covalent C481-binding (ibrutinib, acalabrutinib, zanubrutinib) — C481S-mutation susceptible. Gen 2 = non-covalent reversible (pirtobrutinib/Jaypirca) — C481-agnostic but reversible occupancy. Gen 3 = BTK degraders / PROTACs (C481-agnostic protein elimination): TWO assets now in Phase 3 — (a) bexobrutideg (Nurix NX-5948, Roche-partnered, $700M upfront/$2.3B total) and (b) BeiGene BGB-16673 (CaDAnCe-101 Ph1/2 NCT05006716 → now Ph3 CaDAnCe-302 NCT06846671 + CaDAnCe-303 NCT06970743). Correction vs prior framing: BGB-16673 is no longer Ph2-only — it has advanced to multiple registrational Ph3 trials, so the gen-3 degrader class is a TWO-horse Phase 3 race (Roche/Nurix vs BeiGene), not a single major-pharma entry
